draw_route_proof: logs/rohitg00_k8sgames.draw-proof.log: a directory holding only index.html and draw.html (no vercel.json), served by native SWS 2.38.0 and 2.32.2 with Anybuild's planned flags and no --page-fallback: GET /draw, /draw/ and /draw.html all returned 200 with draw.html's body, /index returned index.html, and /nothere returned 404. So SWS's default behaviour maps an extensionless path to <path>.html; it is not a catch-all fallback and does not come from vercel.json. Wasmer's wasm SWS 2.32.2 build was not tested.
hosting_boundary: vercel.json is Vercel-only. A generic static host (SWS on Wasmer) does not inherit its cache headers or its user-agent redirect that sends AI/SEO crawler user agents (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot, AhrefsBot, ...) to /robots.txt; robots.txt is still served, so compliant crawlers still see its rules, but non-compliant ones are not deflected. The /draw rewrite is not needed on SWS (see draw_route_proof). This is a hosting-behaviour boundary, not an AI-contribution policy. Stated in the README guidance, PR Limitations and here.

why: The README tells people to clone and serve the folder themselves (no install, no build). The game is used to teach Kubernetes, so teams, classes or workshops can host their own fork, for example with their own campaign levels (js/data/CampaignLevels.js) or a translation; #42 shows a community fork doing exactly that for a Korean audience on GitHub Pages. K8s Draw share links are built from window.location.origin, so they point at the self-hosted copy.
